subject: Tier failover and bundle selection — ClearPoint pilot
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood-inference.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@clearpoint.ai>
Cc: procurement@clearpoint.ai
Date: 2027-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Tier failover and bundle selection — ClearPoint pilot

Hi Ellen,

Thanks again for the session yesterday. Per our conversation, I put together two concise options for the pilot you described (30M tokens/month baseline, occasional spikes up to 120M). The two high-level paths are:

1) Throughput-first (Compact+Burst): smaller seat-based bundle with dedicated burst capacity. Lower standing commitment, higher per-spike cost. Fastest path to scale during high-load windows.
2) Feature-first (Full Tier with Addons): larger reserved tier that includes model variants and evaluation tooling (rollout & rollback), better for steady-state predictable cost and built-in audit logging.

A few clarifying questions before we finalize the proposal:
- How long do you expect those spikes to last (minutes, hours, sustained days)?
- Is a soft failover acceptable (automated routing to a cheaper model variant) or do you need guaranteed throughput with fallbacks to other regions?
- Are there compliance constraints for the pilot that would force Private deployment (VPC/on‑prem) vs. Hosted?

I attached a one-page comparison (ClearPoint_MAProposal_v2.pdf) — the section on downgrade windows is page 2. If you prefer, we can model an explicit downgrade/rollback SLA (e.g., 7‑day cooling window with prorated credits) for the pilot.

Next step: if the answers above look good, I’ll loop in Ben and Lauren to land on pricing and the exact seat vs. throughput mix.

Best,
Marcus

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@clearpoint.ai>

Date: 2027-05-23T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tier failover and bundle selection — ClearPoint pilot

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications:

- Spike profile: typically 30–90 minutes, a few times per day (not sustained days).
- Failover expectation: acceptable to route to a cheaper compatible variant for short spikes if we get <500ms extra latency; we need predictable correctness for the top-10 customer flows (no hallucination risk).
- Compliance: hosted is fine for the pilot, but procurement will expect audit logs and an option to push to Private for production.

On downgrade windows: we want a path that doesn’t require 30 days to reduce commitment if the pilot shows demand drop — 7–14 days would be ideal.

Could you also include an example of how credits/offsets would apply if we downgrade mid-quarter? Procurement wants an easy-to-follow example.

Ellen Park
Director of AI Platforms, ClearPoint
ellen.park@clearpoint.ai

Looping you both in — Ellen confirmed spike length (~30–90m), hosted pilot OK, and expects a 7–14 day downgrade window for flexibility. They also asked for a concrete credit example if they need to reduce commitment mid-quarter.

Key asks for pricing note:
- Provide a Compact+Burst example vs Full Tier + Addons (include seat count and throughput mapping for 30M baseline, 120M peak).
- Show pro-rated credit math for a mid-quarter downgrade (example: move from 3-seat reserved to 1-seat reserved after 20 days of the quarter).
- Elastic failover behavior: confirm latency/adaptive routing SLAs and whether we can guarantee the 500ms extra latency threshold for the top flow set.

Ellen — Ben and Lauren will follow up with numbers and the bundle-comparison spreadsheet. Marcus

Subject: Re: Tier failover and bundle selection — ClearPoint pilot (pricing options)

Hi team,

Attached is the bundle-comparison.xlsx — summary below. I kept the math simple so procurement can follow it quickly.

Option A — Compact+Burst (recommended for initial pilot)
- Baseline: 3 reserved seats mapped to 30M tokens/month.
- Burst pool: shared on-demand burst that covers spikes up to 120M (charged per spike token at on-demand rate).
- Downgrade: 7-day cooling window (can reduce seats with prorated credits). Example credit math: quarter = 90 days; reserved seat monthly cost = $6,000. If they drop from 3 -> 1 after 20 days, credit = ((remaining days of month)/days in month) * 2 seats * $6,000. We show a calendar example in the sheet.
- Discount: 15% off list for the pilot term if they commit to a 3-month pilot and provide usage telemetry.
- Failover: routing to quantized variant is supported; measured extra latency ~120–380ms in lab for top flows. We can set a soft SLA: route only if estimated latency <500ms.

Option B — Full Tier + Addons (best for predictable production)
- Baseline: 6 reserved seats + full model family access + audit log addon. Lower per-token price, higher baseline spend.
- Downgrade: 14-day processing window, credits prorated monthly, contract amendment needed for multi-month change.
- Discount: 22% off list for annual commit, 8% for quarterly.

Notes:
- For the pilot I recommend Option A — lower up-front, faster to start, gives ClearPoint the right controls to test spike behavior. If pilot proves steady, transition to Option B with a migration credit (we can credit up to 50% of unused pilot commitments toward the first month of the Full Tier).

I’ll follow up with a short workbook and the sample DocuSign route.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood-inference.com
